es: Comparar dos noticias del mismo hecho y separar hechos, fuentes, grado de certeza y palabras valorativas.

teaching.en: According to the council spokesperson, the festival ended at eight after a power cut, and the crowd left in an orderly way.
teaching.es: Según el portavoz del municipio, el festival terminó a las ocho tras un corte de luz y el público salió de forma ordenada.
teaching.explanationEs: Según + fuente oficial: el dato tiene responsable identificable y un verbo firme (said, confirmed).
segments: According to the council spokesperson, the festival ended at eight after
a power cut, and the crowd left in an orderly way.
teaching.audioText: According to the council spokesperson, the festival ended at eight after a power cut, and the crowd left in an orderly way.

teaching.en: An eyewitness says that hundreds of people panicked when the lights went out, but an anonymous account is harder to check than a named one.
teaching.es: Un testigo presencial dice que cientos de personas entraron en pánico al apagarse las luces, pero un relato anónimo es más difícil de comprobar que uno con nombre.
teaching.explanationEs: Una fuente anónima no se puede verificar; un testigo con nombre, sí, aunque puede equivocarse.
segments: An eyewitness says that hundreds of people panicked when the lights went out,
but an anonymous account is harder to check than a named one.
teaching.audioText: An eyewitness says that hundreds of people panicked when the lights went out, but an anonymous account is harder to check than a named one.

teaching.en: A credible report names its source, gives evidence for every claim and separates the facts from the writer's own opinion.
teaching.es: Una noticia creíble nombra su fuente, da pruebas de cada afirmación y separa los hechos de la opinión del autor.
teaching.explanationEs: Credible = fiable; evidence es incontable (no lleva plural) y claim es una afirmación que hay que respaldar.
segments: A credible report names its source, gives evidence for every
claim and separates the facts from the writer's own opinion.
teaching.audioText: A credible report names its source, gives evidence for every claim and separates the facts from the writer's own opinion.

teaching.en: The council allegedly ignored earlier warnings, yet it has no comment, so the word allegedly keeps the accusation unproved.
teaching.es: El municipio presuntamente ignoró avisos anteriores, pero no hace comentarios, así que la palabra allegedly deja la acusación sin probar.
teaching.explanationEs: Allegedly señala que alguien afirma algo sin pruebas: protege al periodista y deja clara la duda.
segments: The council allegedly ignored earlier warnings, yet it has no
comment, so the word allegedly keeps the accusation unproved.
teaching.audioText: The council allegedly ignored earlier warnings, yet it has no comment, so the word allegedly keeps the accusation unproved.

teaching.en: The organisers insist that nobody was hurt, but some admit that the lights were old, which seems to contradict their first statement.
teaching.es: Los organizadores insisten en que nadie resultó herido, pero algunos admiten que las luces eran viejas, lo que parece contradecir su primera declaración.
teaching.explanationEs: Insist y admit interpretan lo dicho; contradict que algo choca con lo anterior.
segments: The organisers insist that nobody was hurt, but some admit that
the lights were old, which seems to contradict their first statement.
teaching.audioText: The organisers insist that nobody was hurt, but some admit that the lights were old, which seems to contradict their first statement.

teaching.en: When two reports disagree about the number of people or the time, that discrepancy is the first thing to check in a comparison table.
teaching.es: Cuando dos noticias discrepan en el número de personas o en la hora, esa discrepancia es lo primero que hay que comprobar en una tabla comparativa.
teaching.explanationEs: Discrepancy = diferencia entre dos versiones; la tabla separa hecho, fuente, certeza y valoración.
segments: When two reports disagree about the number of people or the time,
that discrepancy is the first thing to check in a comparison table.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión tiene una fuente identificable y por qué es más fiable?

choices.text: The power cut, because an official spokesperson gives it.
The fight, because several fans repeat the same story.
Neither, because both versions are only claims.

feedback.es: El portavoz es una fuente oficial que se puede consultar; los aficionados solo afirman algo sin respaldo.

hint.es: Fíjate en quién aparece nombrado como fuente en cada versión.

origin.text: A spokesperson for the stadium said that the match was stopped because of a power cut. Fans claim that it was stopped because of a fight in the stands.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los organizadores insisten en que nadie resultó herido, pero algunos lo dudan.»

feedback.es: Insist that da a entender que los organizadores mantienen su versión pese a las dudas.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa mantener algo con firmeza; va seguido de that.

origin.text: The organisers ___ that nobody was hurt, but some guests doubt it.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una noticia creíble nombra su fuente y da pruebas.»

answer.text: A credible report names its source and gives evidence

feedback.es: Una noticia creíble se reconoce por dos cosas: la fuente identificada y las pruebas.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto y termina con lo que aporta.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de una noticia con su papel.

pairs: According to a spokesperson, the gates opened at six.
An eyewitness says that the crowd ran.
The report describes the night as chaos.

feedback.es: Cada frase tiene un papel: una fuente oficial, un testigo, una acusación sin probar o una valoración del autor.

pairs: According to a spokesperson, the gates opened at six.
An eyewitness says that the crowd ran.
The report describes the night as chaos.

prompt.es: Escucha la comparación y elige qué hace menos fiable al segundo informe.

choices.text: It includes facts that the other report leaves out completely.
It depends on an unnamed supporter and adds a word of opinion.
It was published before the game had finished.

feedback.es: La fuente anónima no se puede comprobar y «shocking» es una valoración: ambas cosas restan fiabilidad.

origin.audio: Two reports cover the same match. One says that a spokesperson confirmed that the referee stopped the game after a fan ran onto the pitch. The other says that an anonymous supporter claims that the referee was attacked. Only the first gives a source that we can check. The second also uses the word shocking, which is an opinion, not a fact.

prompt.es: Elige la parte de la frase que es un hecho comprobable.

choices.text: The speech was a disaster for the town.
The mayor should have spoken for longer.
Around two hundred people left before the end.

feedback.es: Se puede contar cuánta gente se marchó; «a disaster» es una valoración y «should have» una opinión.

origin.text: The mayor's speech was a disaster for the town, and around two hundred people left before the end.

prompt.es: Lee las dos noticias. ¿Qué sugiere el uso de «Chaos» y «allegedly» en la segunda?

choices.text: That it mixes opinion and unproved accusation with its facts.
That it is more cautious than the first because it names several witnesses.
That it tries to balance both versions by giving the council's reply.

feedback.es: «Chaos» es una valoración y «allegedly» una acusación sin pruebas: la segunda noticia mezcla opinión y dudas con los datos.

origin.text:
Report A: The Riverside Festival ended early on Saturday evening after a power cut, according to a council spokesperson. The spokesperson confirmed that the crowd left in an orderly way and that nobody was hurt. The council says the old cables were checked in April, and it will publish the report next week.
Report B: Chaos at the Riverside Festival! An eyewitness says that hundreds of people panicked when the lights went out, and one anonymous stallholder claims that two people were hurt. The council allegedly ignored warnings about the old cables, but it has no comment.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué fin dice la primera noticia que los cables se revisaron en abril?

choices.text: To show that the council had ignored the problem until that month.
To suggest that the council had already looked after the problem.
To prove that the old cables were the cause of the power cut.

feedback.es: El dato presenta al municipio como previsor, que ya había atendido el problema; no afirma la causa del corte ni lo critica.

origin.text:

The spokesperson confirmed that the crowd left in an orderly way and that nobody was hurt. The council says the old cables were checked in April, and it will publish the report next week.
Report B: Chaos at the Riverside Festival! An eyewitness says that hundreds of people panicked when the lights went out, and one anonymous stallholder claims that two people were hurt. The council allegedly ignored warnings about the old cables, but it has no comment.

prompt.es: Escucha a la reportera y elige qué concluye sobre las dos versiones.

choices.text: That the anonymous guest is lying to get attention.
That the organisers' version is credible because they are official.
That neither version can be trusted until evidence appears.

feedback.es: Dice que no hay pruebas de ninguna de las dos versiones: ni el desmentido de los organizadores ni el invitado anónimo bastan.

origin.audio: A radio reporter compares two accounts of the Riverside Festival. The organisers insist that nobody was hurt and that the crowd left calmly. However, an anonymous guest claims that two people fell in the rush towards the gates. The reporter points out that there is no evidence for either version yet, so she calls the discrepancy the main problem for her own report.

prompt.es: Completa: «La afirmación no es creíble porque depende de un solo invitado anónimo.»

feedback.es: Una afirmación sin fuente comprobable ni pruebas no resulta creíble.

origin.text: The claim is not ___ because it relies on one anonymous guest and offers no evidence.

prompt.es: Lee la carta del lector. ¿Qué critica exactamente?

choices.text: That a serious accusation is printed without naming who makes it.
That the report calls the council guilty without any doubt.
That the paper printed the warnings before checking them.

feedback.es: No niega que la acusación sea cierta: critica que se publique sin decir quién la hace, es decir, sin fuente.

origin.text: Reader's letter: Your report said that the council allegedly ignored warnings, yet you never named who made the accusation. I do not say that it is false, but without a source I cannot take it seriously.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El portavoz admite que las puertas se cerraron tarde.»

answer.text: The spokesperson admits that the gates were closed late

feedback.es: Admit that + oración reconoce algo incómodo; el verbo de la subordinada (were closed) va en pasado.

prompt.es: Completa: «Halló una discrepancia seria entre la cifra oficial y la del testigo.»

feedback.es: Una discrepancy es una diferencia entre dos versiones de un mismo dato; aquí, la cifra oficial frente a la del testigo.

origin.text: The reporter found a serious ___ between the official figure and the eyewitness's estimate of the crowd.
